blocks.text: One of the most important applications of retrosynthesis is in making pharmaceutical products. Many valuable medicines have complex structures, but if they are disconnected properly and efficiently, they can be traced back to very simple, common starting materials.

items: Disconnect the amide C-N bond: the synthons are HO-C6H4-NH- and CH3CO+.
Synthetic equivalents: 4-aminophenol and ethanoyl (acyl) chloride; these are known to react by nucleophilic addition-elimination.
FGI: 4-aminophenol comes from 4-nitrophenol, which is easy to prepare and can be reduced.
Disconnect the C-N bond of 4-nitrophenol: the synthons are the 4-hydroxyphenyl anion and NO2+.
Synthetic equivalents: phenol and nitric acid.

blocks.text: Synthesis: phenol is nitrated to 4-nitrophenol (HNO3), the nitro group is reduced with Sn and HCl to give 4-aminophenol, and this reacts with ethanoyl chloride to give paracetamol, HO-C6H4-NHCOCH3.

blocks.alt: Top: five retrosynthesis steps for paracetamol, from the amide C-N disconnection to phenol and nitric acid. Bottom: phenol with HNO3/H2SO4 gives 4-nitrophenol, Sn + HCl gives 4-aminophenol, and CH3COCl gives paracetamol, HO-C6H4-NHCOCH3.
blocks.caption: Retrosynthesis and synthesis of paracetamol (original diagram after the book's schemes).
blocks.long_description: Working backwards, paracetamol is split at its amide bond, the amine is traced back to a nitro compound, and the nitro compound to phenol. Working forwards, three reactions from earlier chapters, nitration, reduction and acylation, turn phenol into paracetamol.

items: Disconnect the ester C-O bond: the synthons are the 2-carboxyphenoxide ion and CH3CO+.
Synthetic equivalents: salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) and ethanoic (acetic) anhydride.
Disconnect the C-C bond of the carboxyl group in salicylic acid: the synthons are the 2-hydroxyphenyl anion and +COOH.
Synthetic equivalents: phenol and carbon dioxide.

blocks.text: Synthesis: phenol reacts with carbon dioxide at high pressure, and acidification with H2SO4 gives salicylic acid; heating salicylic acid with ethanoic anhydride and an H3PO4 catalyst gives aspirin.

blocks.alt: Top: four retrosynthesis steps for aspirin, from the ester C-O disconnection to salicylic acid and ethanoic anhydride, then the C-C disconnection to phenol and carbon dioxide. Bottom: phenol with (i) CO2 at high temperature and pressure and (ii) H2SO4 gives salicylic acid; with (CH3CO)2O, H3PO4 and heat it gives aspirin.
blocks.caption: Retrosynthesis and synthesis of aspirin (original diagram after the book's schemes).
blocks.long_description: Aspirin is an ester of salicylic acid. Disconnecting the ester leads to salicylic acid, and disconnecting its carboxyl group leads to phenol and CO2. In the forward direction CO2 is added to the ring of phenol, and the OH group of salicylic acid is then acetylated by ethanoic anhydride.

items: Aspirin and paracetamol are both made from phenol. What is the overall functional group difference between them?
Which FGI is involved in their syntheses?
Which synthon is common to both preparations? Give its structure and its usual synthetic equivalent.
